messages.text: Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

Great question — this is actually one of the Rev 6.1's deliberate design wins.

**The onboard F1 fuse takes the hit, not the miner.**

There's a small automotive-style blade fuse (the "yellow fuse") mounted **right on the board**, beside the XT30 power input. If a spike comes in:

- The F1 fuse blows first — sacrificing itself
- The B.1370 chips and electronics behind it are protected
- You replace a cheap fuse, not a $249 miner

**Why this matters:** cheaper home miners skip this entirely. A spike there goes straight into the board — and as the designer put it, *"they fail and then they could kill the power supply or they kill the miner with it."*

The included **350 W MEANWELL PSU** also helps — it's loafing at ~30% load feeding a ~100 W miner, so it's running calm and stable, not stressed.

No protection is absolute, but the Rev 6.1 has a proper sacrificial fuse where it counts. 🛡️
What voltage and frequency does it come with

Straight from the verified benchmarks:

- **Core voltage:** ~1,250 mV (1.25 V) to the BM1370 chips
- **Input voltage:** 12 V (via the MEANWELL LRS-350-12 PSU)
- **Stock frequency:** **800 MHz** — the recommended sweet spot

At those settings you get **~6 TH/s @ ~103 W**, with the input holding steady at **11.9 V** (no sag, thanks to the XT30 connector + thicker PCB).

There's also an **eco mode at 600 MHz** (~4.82 TH/s @ ~71 W) if you want to run leaner — most efficient mode at **~14.7 J/TH**.

Both are adjustable via the **AxeOS web dashboard** — no special tools needed.
Is the included power supply actually reliable?

Yes — and it's genuinely one of the better inclusions at this price point.

**The M. LRS-350-12 at a glance:**
- 350 W / 29 A rated, **UL/CE/UKCA certified** — industrial-grade supply
- The miner draws ~100 W stock, so it's **loafing at ~30% of its cap····**
- A supply running that cool and relaxed lasts a long time

**Why that matters:**
Many competitors bundle ~99–124 W bricks running near their limit 24/7. As the designer put it — those are *"very likely to fail running the miner twenty four seven"* and can take the miner with them when they go.

This one has serious headroom. It's the **same PSU proven to handle overclock runs well past stock draw** in lab testing.

**Bottom line:** it's not a throwaway brick — it's an oversized industrial supply deliberately chosen so it never breaks a sweat at stock settings, and has room if you ever want to push harder later.
